Subject: Quick post-call recap + next steps on residency pricing

Hi Liam — thanks again for your time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

1) Usage profile: you indicated 6–12M tokens/month initially, moving to ~30M in 6–9 months with heavy chat + summarization workloads.
2) Residency requirement: Vault Finance needs data stored and processed in the EU for production (pilot can be in hosted us-west for testing).
3) Target economics: you called out an internal benchmark of $900–$1,200 per 1M tokens as an acceptable run-rate target for production.

What Im proposing: 
- Pilot (4 weeks): hosted EU region with small reserved concurrency to validate latency/SLOs and integration. Cost estimate: $1,600 per 1M tokens (pilot configuration, includes reserved baseline + regional premium).
- Production target: with Dedicated capacity + batching and prefix caching we can approach $1,000 per 1M tokens at ~30M/month. Exact $/1M depends on batch tuning, KV cache hit rate, and quantization.

Next steps I recommend: 
- Well run a short cost sensitivity table for Vaults 6/12/30M scenarios (I attached a one-page playbook).
- You share any specific compliance docs beyond SOC 2 (if FISMA/PCI is relevant, flag it).
- Internal call next Wednesday 10am CET to review the sensitivity table and discuss a pilot scope + duration.

Attachments: Redwood_Regional_Pricing_Playbook_v1.pdf (summary), SOC2_Summary_for_VaultFin.docx (excerpt).

Cheers,
Hannah Schmitt

- Residency: EU production is a hard requirement. Pilot can be EU as well if the latency looks OK; concerned about a regional premium that makes the unit-econ impossible.

Hannah / Ben — notes for the sensitivity table and the ask from Liam:

1) Baseline hosted EU: use our standard hosted eu list price for the conversational model (v2) = $1,800 / 1M tokens (no reserve).
2) Small Dedicated profile (reserve ~2x concurrency of pilot): expected delta is -20% from hosted eu list once steady-state (i.e., ~$1,440 / 1M) assuming we can enable continuous batching + 35% KV hit.
3) Aggressive dedicated + quantization at scale (30M): can approach $950–$1,050 / 1M but will require a 3-month ramp and model/precision validation.
4) Cache sensitivity: provide columns for 0% / 20% / 40% KV cache hit; at 40% expect a ~15% reduction in token cost vs the baseline dedicated number.
5) Latency: EU 95p with hosted eu: ~220–300ms; dedicated optimized: 120–180ms (depends on sequence length and batch policy).

Ill draft the sensitivity table and include two flavors: pilot-conservative (hosted eu pilot) and accelerated (dedicated pilot with canary). Hannah — want to confirm the call slot Wed 10am CET? Ill invite procurement/solutions engineering as needed.
